---
title: "Output Files"
description: "The formats of the INTEGRATOR result files written to the project folder"
---

INTEGRATOR writes its results to the project folder as plain CSV tables, a binary results
folder, and — optionally — chromatogram PDFs. The CSV files are the interface to downstream
tools.

::: {.compact-table}
| File | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| [`long.csv`](#long.csv) | Step 3 | Long-format peak table, one row per *sample × feature*. |
| [`quant_raw.csv`](#quant_raw.csv) | Step 3 | Wide-format peak-area matrix (samples × features). |
| [`RT_matrix.csv`](#rt_matrix.csv) | Step 2 | Per-sample integration borders; editable for manual per-peak adjustment. |
| [`misc/`](#misc) | Step 3 | Binary results, read by MRMhub-viz and step 4. |
| [PDF folders](#chromatogram-pdfs) | Step 4 | Chromatogram PDFs (optional). |
:::

All CSV tables are plain comma-separated files. See the
[Processing Workflow](running.qmd) for the steps that produce them.

## long.csv

Long format: one row per *sample × feature*, for every integrated peak. Only `feature_name`
and `raw_data_filename` (plus at least one intensity column) are essential; the remaining
columns are metadata and measurements carried through for downstream processing. Columns, in
file order:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `feature_name` | Feature (analyte) identifier — the feature name from the feature list, or the compound name where no feature name is given. |
| `internal_standard` | Assigned ISTD feature, from the feature list. |
| `raw_data_filename` | Source mzML file name; becomes the analysis identifier. |
| `time_stamp` | Acquisition timestamp, read from the mzML. |
| `batch` | Batch identifier, from `run_order.csv`. |
| `sample_type` | Sample / QC type, from `run_order.csv`. |
| `precursor_mz` | Precursor-ion *m/z*. |
| `product_mz` | Product-ion *m/z*. |
| `collision_energy` | Collision energy. |
| `polarity` | Ionisation polarity (`+` / `−`). |
| `rt_apex` | Retention time at the peak apex (min). |
| `area` | Integrated peak area. |
| `height` | Peak height above the integration baseline at the apex (see below). |
| `FWHM` | Full width at half maximum (min), above the integration baseline (see below); empty if it cannot be measured. |
| `rt_int_start` | Left integration border (min). |
| `rt_int_end` | Right integration border (min). |
| `trace_cut_pct` | Peak truncated by the end of the acquired MRM trace (see below); empty otherwise. |
| `sn_ratio` | Signal-to-noise ratio: `height` divided by the noise of the baseline around the peak (see below). |
| `noise_method` | Noise estimate used for `sn_ratio`: `robust`, `rms` or `p2p` (set by `sn_noise` in `param.txt`). |

Where no peak was found for a *sample × feature*, the measurement fields
(`rt_apex`…`noise_method`) are left empty.

`height` and `FWHM` are measured from the integration baseline at the apex, i.e. the baseline that
the selected baseline mode uses for the area (the 5th-percentile level, the `v_drop` level, or the
valley-to-valley line). `height` is the apex intensity minus that baseline. `FWHM` is the time
between the first point on the left and the last point on the right at which the trace crosses
half of that height, inside the integration window and interpolated linearly between data points;
if the window contains several peaks above half height, the width spans all of them. `FWHM` is left
empty when the trace does not fall below half height before a window edge, i.e. when the peak is
cut by the integration window.

`trace_cut_pct` flags peaks that are cut off by the end of the acquired trace, e.g. when a
scheduled MRM window closes before the peak has returned to baseline. It is filled when the
integration window reaches the first or last data point of the trace, and gives the signal at
that point as a percentage of the apex height, both above the baseline (the 5th percentile of the
whole trace, for every baseline mode):

- **negative** values: cut at the start of the trace; **positive** values: cut at the end;
- **±100**: the apex itself lies on the trace end;
- **empty**: the integration window does not reach a trace end, the signal there is at or below
  baseline, or no peak was found.

If the window reaches both trace ends, the larger value is reported, with its sign. The column is
left empty when `crop_window` is set, because the stored trace then ends at the crop limits rather
than at the end of the acquired trace. It is recomputed in step 3, so it follows manual changes to
the integration borders in `RT_matrix.csv`.

`sn_ratio` is the peak `height` divided by the noise of the trace in a region around the peak. The
region extends 10 × FWHM to each side of the apex (20 × FWHM in total) and excludes the integration
windows of all features of the same transition; if `FWHM` is empty, the integration-window width
divided by 3.5 is used in place of FWHM. The noise is estimated from the intensities in this region
according to `sn_noise` in `param.txt`:

| `noise_method` | Noise | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `robust` (default) | 1.4826 × median absolute deviation, after removing other peaks | Other peaks in the region (e.g. isomers or isotopic interferences that are not features of the transition) are removed first: points more than 3 × the noise above the median are discarded repeatedly, as in OpenMS, but at most half of the region. Insensitive to neighbouring peaks, peak tails and spikes. |
| `rms` | Standard deviation | The RMS noise of most vendor software; inflated by any peak in the region. |
| `p2p` | (maximum − minimum) / 2 | Gives the pharmacopoeia ratio 2*H*/*h* (USP ⟨621⟩, Ph. Eur. 2.2.46); the most sensitive to spikes and neighbouring peaks. |

The noise is at least 1. `sn_ratio` is rounded to one decimal and is 0 for a peak that does not rise
above its baseline. It is left empty when fewer than 10 data points remain in the region (e.g. in a
short scheduled MRM window), and, with `crop_window`, the region is limited to the stored part of the
trace. Values from different methods, or from vendor software (which often smooths the trace first),
are not interchangeable. `sn_ratio` is measured within each sample and describes peak quality; it is
not a detection or quantification limit, which pharmacopoeias and ICH Q2(R2) base on blank samples.

An empty `sn_ratio` is read as `NA` in R, and `dplyr::filter(sn_ratio >= 10)` drops those rows as
well; use `filter(is.na(sn_ratio) | sn_ratio >= 10)` to keep them.

## quant_raw.csv

A wide matrix of peak areas: one column per feature, one row per sample, preceded by header
rows. It carries areas only. The first column holds the row labels:

| | *feature 1* | *feature 2* | … |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | LPC 20:4 | PC 34:1 | … |
| `precursor` | 544.3 | 760.6 | … |
| `product` | 184.1 | 184.1 | … |
| `RT` | 4.21 | 6.05 | … |
| *sample01.mzML* | 15234.0 | 88213.0 | … |
| *sample02.mzML* | … | … | … |

The `RT` row is the **expected** retention time from the feature list (not the peak apex);
each sample row holds that sample's integrated peak area per feature.

## RT_matrix.csv

Produced in step 2: a wide matrix of the per-sample integration borders. It can be edited to
adjust individual peaks by hand; re-running **step 3 only** re-integrates with the edited
bounds (see [Processing Workflow — step 2](running.qmd#step-2-peak-detection-and-rt-shift-estimation)).

Layout: each sample is a row, and each feature occupies **two adjacent columns** — its left
and right integration border, as an absolute retention time in that sample (min). Two header
rows identify the columns, and a blank spacer column separates the transition groups:

- Header row 1 — the transition (`compound / transition`), repeated over each feature's
  border pair.
- Header row 2 — `compound name`, then each feature's name over its border pair.
- One row per mzML file — the file name, then the left and right border for each feature.

::: {.callout-important}
## Step 2 overwrites `RT_matrix.csv`
Make a backup of `RT_matrix.csv` before re-running Step 2 in case you manually edited `RT_matrix.csv`, as step 2 **overwrites all manual edits!**
:::

## Folder 'misc/' {#misc}

A folder of binary result files written during step 3. It is consumed by the
[MRMhub-viz](viz.qmd) visualiser and by step-4 PDF generation, and is not intended for direct
reading. If the folder is removed, MRMhub-viz and step 4 cannot run until step 3 is repeated.

## Chromatogram PDFs

Optional, written by step 4 into three folders:

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `by_transition/` | One PDF per transition, over all samples with a peak above the minimum-intensity threshold. |
| `by_transition_low/` | Transitions with no peak above the threshold (`low_intensity_threshold` in `MRMhub_plot.r`). |
| `by_sample/` | One PDF per reference sample, with all its transitions. |
